messages:
li: Quick heads-up — autotune sweep found a perf regression on sm92 with INT4 for seqlen >= 2048. baseline kernel pick used int4_fast_gemm but latency jumped ~18% after we applied the new tie-break weight.

matt: Can you paste the perf numbers? single-run or aggregate?

li: aggregate p50/p95 over 5 runs:

```
model: 7B-qlo
seqlen: 2048
arch: sm92
quant: INT4
old_pick: int4_safe_gemm (p50=42ms p95=78ms)
new_pick: int4_fast_gemm (p50=50ms p95=92ms)
```

anya: Oof. Was KV cache warmup the same across runs? int4_fast_gemm has larger workspace; it may trigger a different kv cache allocation path.

li: yes, same warmup. Noticed higher L2 thrashing—profiling shows >2x local mem write stall on int4_fast_gemm.

sara: Maybe we need per-arch hysteresis + seqlen breakpoint. For sm92 prefer safe_gemm when seqlen >= 1024 unless batch_size >= 4.

julia: I can add a small priority matrix in autotuner: keys = [arch,seqlen_bucket, batch_bucket, quant] -> pick + penalty. simple JSON config.

li: Thanks — example config I sketched:

```
{"rules":[
  {"arch":"sm92","seqlen":">=1024","quant":"INT4","preferred":"int4_safe_gemm","penalty":"0.05"},
  {"arch":"sm90","seqlen":"<512","quant":"FP8","preferred":"fp8_fp_fast","penalty":"0.02"}
]}
```

matt: +1. Also add kv-cache warmup flag so autotuner measures after kv priming, not cold-start. Add a metric 'kv_hit_ratio' to the selection objective.

dev-bot: autotune job 1822004600 completed (success). logs: /ci/autotune/1822004600

sara: We'll run a targeted sweep with the matrix and compare p50/p95 across seqlen buckets. li, can you capture a perf trace for the int4_fast_gemm run (nsight or nvprof)?

li: Uploading trace now. link: https://internal/share/trace-18220

matt: If regression persists, fallback hysteresis: only switch to fast_gemm if 10% improvement sustained across 3 consecutive runs. prevents flapping.

julia: I'll implement tie-break logic + kv priming in autotuner this week. planning to roll to staging on Thursday.

li: great, thanks — will watch staging perf dashboards. :thumbsup:
